items.followUp: How does increasing temperature affect the rate of diffusion?

rubric.why: After the first electron is removed, the second electron is removed from a positive ion rather than a neutral atom.
rubric.description: States that the second electron is removed from a positive ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the ion as positive.

rubric.why: The remaining electrons experience greater attraction to the nucleus, so removing the next electron requires more energy.
rubric.description: Explains that the remaining electrons are held more strongly and the second electron is harder to remove.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the increased attraction or energy required.

modelAnswer: After the first electron is removed, the atom becomes a positive ion.
The remaining electrons are attracted more strongly to the nucleus, so more energy is needed to remove the second electron than the first.

items.followUp: Define an ionic bond and give one example.

rubric.why: Sharing electron pairs between atoms is the defining feature of a covalent bond.
rubric.description: Defines a covalent bond as a bond formed by sharing one or more pairs of electrons between atoms.

rubric.why: A valid example demonstrates a substance with covalent bonds.
rubric.description: Gives one correct example of a covalent substance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is a chemical bond formed when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons.
For example, the bond between the two hydrogen atoms in H₂ is covalent.

items.followUp: Name four factors that affect the rate of evaporation.

rubric.why: Identifying any two factors earns the first mark.
rubric.description: Names at least two factors that affect diffusion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any two correct factors.

rubric.why: The question asks for four factors; identifying all four earns the second mark.
rubric.description: Names all four factors: temperature, concentration gradient, particle size and nature of the medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when all four factors are named.

modelAnswer: Four factors that affect diffusion are temperature, concentration gradient, particle size and the nature of the medium.

items.followUp: Define a saturated solution and give one example.

rubric.why: An aqueous solution is defined by water being its solvent.
rubric.description: Defines an aqueous solution as a solution in which water is the solvent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that water is the solvent.

rubric.why: A correct example shows a substance dissolved in water.
rubric.description: Gives one valid example of an aqueous solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

modelAnswer: An aqueous solution is a solution in which water is the solvent.
For example, sodium chloride dissolved in water forms an aqueous solution.
